headline: Europe shrugs off Seoul's sell-off as Germany's PMI surprises and a cold snap lifts gas

findings.headline: German PMI at a 56-month high splits the eurozone in two
findings.body: November's flash PMIs had Germany's composite at 55.0, its best since March 2022, with factory output at a 63-month high and factory hiring back for the first time in nearly three and a half years. France fell further to 46.2, so the eurozone composite only held at 51.7. German cost inflation eased but stays historically elevated, which keeps the ECB from leaning dovish just as the Fed debate turns softer.

findings.headline: Cold-snap forecasts meet thin storage in European gas
findings.body: The Dutch front month spiked as high as €96.08 before giving back about half the gain, on forecasts of a cold and less windy north-west Europe into early December. EU storage is only about 69% full, well below the usual level for late November, after slower Qatari supply and heavy summer cooling demand. If the cold holds, withdrawals speed up and the risk shifts to late-winter scarcity, which feeds straight into power prices.

findings.headline: Seoul readies its 2008-era fund but Europe declines to follow Asia
findings.body: The KOSPI fell 3.31% after Friday's rout, and Korea is preparing its 10.76 trillion won stock-market stabilisation fund for the first time in 18 years, though it has not been deployed. European chip and tech names are leading rather than lagging, so the overnight AI selling has not carried into Europe's morning. Whether that holds depends on the US open and Wednesday's PCE data.

sources.label: Korea MOFE: emergency market review meeting, 22 Nov
Korea Herald: Can 2008-era tool stop the latest market rout?

view: Our view: the overnight AI scare has not travelled to Europe, and Germany's recovery gives Europe a reason to keep leading; the risk to that is energy, because a cold, still December with storage this low would hit the same German industry the PMI just flagged.
